questions.q: What is the meaning of the term 'Collage' in art?
options: A technique of drawing realistic portraits with a pencil.
An art technique that involves gluing various materials to a flat surface to create a picture.
A method of carving figures out of stone.
The process of dyeing fabrics in a chemical bath.
questions.explain: Derived from the French word 'coller' meaning 'to glue', Collage is a technique where different materials like paper, photographs, and fabric are pasted onto a backing surface.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Which of the following is an indispensable material required for producing a collage?
questions.explain: Because a collage relies entirely on sticking assorted materials to a flat board or canvas, an adhesive (like glue or gum) is the most critical binding material.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: When distinguishing collage from painting, which characteristic primarily defines a collage?
options: It is created solely by applying wet pigments with a brush.
It must be done on a rounded 3D surface like a vase.
It is composed of mixed media such as cut-outs, fabrics, and magazine clips.
It requires the use of hot wax to resist colors.
questions.explain: A collage relies on assembling disparate materials (mixed media) like cut paper, fabric, and objects onto a surface, unlike painting which applies wet color to a surface.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Which set of tools and materials is perfectly suited for making a basic classroom collage?
options: Old magazines, scissors, gum, and cardboard
questions.explain: Old magazines provide the visual elements, scissors cut them, gum acts as the adhesive, and cardboard provides the flat support surface for the collage.
